candidates.exact_span:
It is proposed that the permit be reissued for a 5-year term following regulations promulgated at
40 CFR §122.46(a). This is a renewal of an existing permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether FY2025 discharge limits and monitoring requirements are governed by the reissued permit versus the prior permit depends on how the proposed 5-year renewal term and continuity of an existing permit are interpreted for the evaluation period.

candidates.exact_span:
Regulations contained in 40 CFR §122.44 require that NPDES permit limits are developed that
meet the more stringent of either technology-based effluent limitation guidelines, numerical
and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits, or the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable enforceable limit for each parameter depends on which of the three sources is selected as most stringent and how narrative versus numerical WQS-based limits participate in that comparison; different readings change which limit is used for exceedance determinations.

candidates.exact_span: Technology-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for TSS.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage identifies TSS as subject to technology-based effluent limitations rather than WQBEL or report-only monitoring; interpreting whether those limitations are operative and enforceable for FY2025 changes whether reported TSS measurements are compared to a numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span:
Water quality-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for pH and
TRC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage assigns pH and TRC to water-quality-based rather than technology-based limits; different interpretations of what WQBELs are established and whether they are numeric or narrative change the applicable compliance comparison for those parameters.

candidates.exact_span:
Regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.44 (a) require technology-based effluent limitations to
be placed in NPDES permits based on ELGs where applicable, on BPJ in the absence of
guidelines, or on a combination of the two.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether technology-based limits derive from ELGs, BPJ, or a combination affects which underlying standards and derivation method apply, which can change the enforceable numeric limit selected for parameters such as TSS.

candidates.exact_span:
In the absence of promulgated guidelines for the
discharge, permit conditions may be established using BPJ procedures.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If the discharge is interpreted as lacking applicable ELGs, limits may be set by BPJ rather than guideline-based values; that determination changes which numeric limit is applicable for technology-based parameters.

candidates.exact_span:
numerical
and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting whether a parameter is governed by numerical versus narrative WQS-based limits determines whether an ordinary numeric compliance comparison applies (Purpose A) and how missing or non-numeric reported results should be classified when no numeric limit is operative (Purpose C).
